title: Resource Slicing for Time-Sensitive Data Traffic in Non-Terrestrial Networks with FSO ISLs
comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops
summary: In multi-hop Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, time-sensitive packets experience queueing across multiple satellite hops, causing per-hop waiting times that accumulate and make the maximum end-to-end (E2E) delay difficult to guarantee. This paper presents a novel multi-hop slicing framework that reserves time-frequency resources for each time-sensitive flow of data originating at each satellite, aiming to maintain the reservation of communication resources along every inter-satellite link (ISL) on its route to the ground station (GS). The number of time-frequency resource blocks (RBs) reserved per-hop is determined from the data packet arrival statistics, E2E delay budget, and target level of reliability. Reservations on consecutive links are temporally aligned to enable pipelined forwarding of the time-sensitive data flows aggregated from terrestrial user terminals on the different LEO satellites. We evaluate the proposed framework against conventional scheduling and resource-allocation baselines, including pure time-division multiple access (Pure-TDMA), first-in-first-out (FIFO), and farthest-satellite-first (FSF), over the same multi-hop LEO satellite path. Under light traffic conditions, the baseline schemes provide comparable delay performance; however, their high-percentile delays increase sharply as data traffic load grows, whereas the proposed framework exhibits substantially slower delay growth. At the high arrival rate and high reliability target considered, the proposed scheme requires about 31 ms, a factor of 2.5-6.8 lower than the 76, 180, and 210 ms required by FIFO, FSF, and Pure-TDMA.

title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.

title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
summary: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.

title: Resilience in Wireless: A Lyapunov-Constrained Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Approach
summary: Traditional wireless networks mainly use reliability metrics to evaluate network stability. However, reliable data delivery alone cannot fully characterize network stability under variations in wireless environments and physical tasks. Wireless network resilience provides a broader perspective by describing the ability to maintain acceptable service and recover from disruptions. We develop an integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) framework that incorporates communication reliability and sensing error into a state-dependent Lyapunov constraint for adaptive BS beamforming. The resulting transmit-power minimization problem is non-convex and solved via semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation with rank-one recovery. We establish conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness, while simulations demonstrate improved resilience and faster recovery over a static baseline.

title: Type-based Over-the-Air Computation
comment: Manuscript submitted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications
summary: Over-the-air computation (OAC) exploits the superposition property of wireless channels to compute functions of distributed data, reducing the communication overhead associated with its multiple access. However, existing OAC frameworks are often designed around specific classes of functions, limiting their applicability to more general nonlinear computations. This paper investigates type-based multiple access (TBMA) as a general framework for OAC, enabling the receiver to recover a histogram of the distributed observations and compute a broad class of functions without modifying the underlying communication scheme. We formulate TBMA as a histogram estimation problem and propose two digital detectors. We prove that a low-complexity successive cancellation algorithm achieves the optimal maximum-likelihood (ML) performance. We derive analytical expressions for the mean squared error (MSE) and compare TBMA with conventional schemes in terms of computation accuracy, transmission duration, bandwidth and energy consumption. Numerical experiments validate the analytical results and demonstrate that, unlike existing OAC techniques, TBMA exhibits an exponential MSE decay with increasing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and constant transmit energy, independently of the function being computed. These findings position TBMA as a step toward more versatile OAC architectures, compatible with existing transmission schemes, and broadening the range of functions that can be computed directly over the wireless channel and enabling new possibilities for distributed computation and decision-making.

title: An Evidence-Guided Framework for Tissue-Barrier Impedance Review: Deletion and Resistance Sensitivity
summary: Reviewing tissue-barrier impedance requires connecting spectral anomalies with resistance estimates and experimental context. We present an evidence-guided framework that coordinates numerical checks and traceable actions for human review. In-house simulations assess the effect of removing flagged frequencies, public datasets test model adaptation, and local measurements demonstrate the review workflow. Removing flagged frequencies reduced resistance error under quadratic objectives, whereas robust fitting showed little average benefit from deletion and a mean error increase for endpoint-pair perturbations. High errors clustered around a few fitted circuit parameter sets, highlighting the value of examining parameter identifiability. Under the tested noise and perturbation conditions, these findings support robust full-spectrum estimation, flag-guided inspection, and matched sensitivity checks.

title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
summary: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.

title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures; 12-page supplement included. Supplementary Data 1-9 (CSV) are provided as ancillary files
summary: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.

title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Includes supplementary material. Published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering. Code: https://github.com/MLI-lab/fetal_magnetocardiography
summary: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.

title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, roughly half of the gain of an idealized reference.

title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 1st Annual Integrated Sensing and Communication Conference (ISAC)
summary: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.
